light_description: Organic Sounds' first original fuzz; three-position rotary gain control, developed as a compact vintage-oriented fuzz/booster. Official product page carries multiple exterior images.
Limited Kerberos variant adding Master Volume and vintage-part selection; retained as a substantive edition relationship because controls and parts presentation differ from the one-control Kerberos.
Organic Sounds fuzz built to pursue the feel of a vintage Fuzz Face; surviving dealer documentation provides exterior imagery and identifies separate germanium and silicon variants.
Germanium-transistor Orthros production variant; retained as a generation/component variant because surviving documentation explicitly identifies it as a distinct version.
Silicon-transistor Orthros production variant; retained separately from the germanium version for specimen identification.
Compact Organic Sounds fuzz based on the builder's vintage Big Muff Ram's Head reference work; official overseas page supplies six exterior photographs and detailed product information.
Organic Sounds reconstruction of the Burns BUZZAROUND based on the builder's own vintage specimen and distinctive enclosure; official overseas catalog provides product imagery and historical context.
Organic Sounds reconstruction of the ELKA DIZZY TONE based on the builder's own original; official overseas catalog preserves the model as part of its vintage series.
Organic Sounds vintage-series Fuzz Face-oriented model family; current overseas catalog includes germanium and silicon-labeled variants with exterior imagery.
Organic Sounds vintage-style fuzz using OC75 germanium transistors; current product catalog provides exterior product imagery and product identity.
Good Feeling Drive, a guitar/bass distortion using FET stages rather than an IC; official documentation gives launch date, controls and exterior product presentation.
ALBIT distortion/booster model documented in the official effectors catalog; retained as a named dirt product pending deeper historical chronology.
Bass-oriented ALBIT distortion/booster model documented in the official effectors catalog; retained as a separate model identity.
ALBIT distortion/booster model documented in the official effectors catalog; retained pending deeper historical and specimen reconciliation.
ALBIT guitar-oriented custom booster/distortion family record documented in the official catalog.
ALBIT bass-oriented custom booster/distortion family record documented in the official catalog.
TubeSound Booster / overdrive booster using six FETs to approximate tube characteristics; official page documents 2015 release, controls and enclosure dimensions.
Bass version of the TubeSound Booster family documented in ALBIT's official effectors catalog.
ALBIT distortion/booster model appearing in the official current/historical effectors catalog; retained as a named product record pending chronology and specimen reconciliation.
Bass overdrive designed around two gain controls and two filter paths, with low/high-gain operation; official documentation identifies it as discontinued.
ALBIT named distortion/booster model preserved from the official catalog; deeper historical and photo reconciliation remains queued.
ALBIT named distortion/booster model preserved from the official catalog; deeper historical and photo reconciliation remains queued.
Germanium Diode Fuzz for Guitar, introduced in 2021; official page documents germanium-diode construction, controls, dimensions and product imagery.
Bass version of the Germanium Diode Fuzz family; official page documents the bass model separately with the same named control architecture.
Bass fuzz with separate high/low gain controls and a frequency-balancing design target; official page documents its 2012 release and discontinued status.
Micro FUZZ from the SKULL series with Gate and Master-style controls; official page documents its 2012 release, compact enclosure and discontinued status.
Historical OverDrive Fuzz / fuzz-driver documented in an ALBIT manual, combining fuzz and drive behavior with a multi-control switching layout; retained as a historical catalog record.
